About

A little about me

I'm Menna'Allah, a UI/UX designer based in Egypt. I enjoy taking problems with a lot of moving pieces — trip planning, gym memberships, plant care questions — and shaping them into interfaces that feel simple and calm to use. My favorite part of the process is usually the small decisions: a color palette with real meaning behind it, a feature that solves one specific frustration, a flow with one less step than it needs.

My recent work spans travel & archaeology, fitness, food, and community-driven product design — including Kemet, a team project presented to Egypt's Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities. I'm currently open to UI/UX roles — product, agency, or freelance — where I can keep working on real, detail-driven problems.

Case studies

The full breakdown

Problem, process, and outcome for each project above.

Flagship — Mobile App

Kemet — Travel & Archaeology Guide

Team of 5 · Egypt travel & archaeology · Role: UI Designer

The problem. Tourists exploring Egypt's archaeological sites face a fragmented experience — reliable site information, trip planning, trusted guides, and local recommendations are scattered across unreliable sources and guesswork.

The solution. Kemet consolidates the entire trip into one place: site information, smooth trip planning, personalized suggestions for restaurants and hotels, a list of qualified tour guides, and a space for travelers to share tips and stories with each other.

Recognition. Kemet was presented to the Ministry and stood out as one of the strongest projects in its cohort.

My role

UI Designer on a 5-person team. I led the color palette and contributed to many of the app's core features.

Team

All 5 team members were designers, splitting research, flows, and visual design across the app.

Process

The color palette draws directly from ancient Egyptian heritage — gold, the color pharaohs decorated themselves and their jewelry with, paired with blue from the Nile.

Key features I designed

  • Scan: scan the QR code on an artifact to pull up its information, with an audio option.
  • Community: travelers share their own experiences and stories from each site.

Outcome

Presented to the Ministry as one of the standout projects in its cohort.

FitPlan+ — Fitness & Training App

Solo project · Gym & personal training · Role: UI Designer (end to end)

The problem. Choosing a gym plan and a private trainer can be confusing and impersonal — pricing tiers are hard to compare, and there's no clear path from picking a plan to actually tracking a workout.

The solution. FitPlan+ lets users browse gyms and private trainers, pick the plan that fits them, and move straight into a clean, motivating in-app training experience.

My role

Sole designer on the project — I designed the Plans & Pricing page and the full in-app look, including the workout tracking screens.

Key screens

  • Plans & Pricing: three-tier comparison (Basic, Premium, VIP) with a clear "most popular" highlight to guide the decision.
  • Workout summary: exercise cards with reps, weight, and thumbnails, plus a single clear "Let's Start" action.

PureRoots — Healthy Food Restaurant Website

Solo project · Restaurant & healthy eating · Role: UI Designer (full website)

The problem. A restaurant built around fresh, wholesome food needs a website that makes that feeling obvious the moment it loads — not a generic template that could belong to any restaurant.

The solution. A full website for PureRoots covering the homepage, menu highlights, an about/welcome section introducing the kitchen, and contact/footer — built entirely solo, from layout to final visuals.

My role

Sole designer — responsible for every page: homepage, menu highlights, about section, and footer.

Process

Chose a nature-inspired green palette to reinforce the "pure" in PureRoots, paired with warm food photography to keep it appetizing rather than clinical.

Plantrest — Plant Care & Inspiration App

Personal project · Plant care & community · Role: UI Designer (concept to logo to product)

The problem. Plant owners often have specific questions about their plants — light, watering, care — with no easy place to ask people who actually know.

The solution. Plantrest — the name combines "Plant" and "Pinterest" — is a self-initiated app for plant inspiration and care, browsable by category (indoor, low light, easy care), with detailed plant pages and a community feature where owners can ask questions and get answers from experienced plant people.

My role

Entirely self-initiated — I came up with the name, designed and hand-drew the logo, and designed the product end to end.

Key feature I designed

Community: a space for people with plant questions to get answers from people with hands-on experience.
